slides.title: Evaluate a synthetic service chain on OpenShift.

narration.text: The purpose is to evaluate whether a small set of components can be deployed and connected in a controlled proof of concept.
The scope is deliberately limited to the recorded synthetic environment.
This exercise provides a deployment baseline for later decisions, with further validation required before any production claim is made.

slides.title: Validate HTTP reachability without claiming authenticated workflows.

narration.text: The test plan uses direct HTTP requests to selected endpoints and records the response outcome for each scenario.
It does not log in as an end user, submit a complete authenticated transaction, or exercise authorization boundaries.
These distinctions matter when interpreting a passing endpoint check alongside the broader project objective.

slides.title: Preserve original checks and identify incomplete validation.

narration.text: The execution record keeps the original scenario identities and observed statuses together.
A missing execution must be labeled incomplete instead of being counted as a pass.
This synthetic run contains three executed checks and no incomplete scenario, but the reporting rule still prevents future missing observations from becoming invented successful results.

slides.title: The planned frontend sends requests to an API service.

narration.text: The planned synthetic frontend sends requests to an API service across the documented service boundary.
The setup is a declared acceptance fixture rather than a discovered customer deployment.
Its purpose is to exercise an evidence-backed explanation of component relationships, with each relationship tied to this retained report and without inventing a distributed trace.

slides.title: The API queues work for a separate background worker.

narration.text: The API places work on a queue for a separate background worker.
This separation lets the synthetic design describe the request-facing component and the asynchronous processing component independently.
The queue relationship belongs to the declared setup evidence.
It should not be interpreted as a measured latency result, a throughput benchmark, or an authenticated transaction.

slides.title: The worker writes synthetic records to a storage service.

narration.text: The background worker writes synthetic records to a storage service after processing queued work.
The report records that relationship as part of the fixture setup.

A storage endpoint check can support reachability, while durability, backup behavior, restore procedures, and behavior after a component restart still require separate tests before the system can be treated as production ready.

slides.title: Quay holds the UBI images used by the Kubernetes deployment.

narration.text: Quay stores the UBI based container images referenced by the Kubernetes deployment on OpenShift.
This statement describes the synthetic setup and image distribution path.
It does not claim that image scanning, signature enforcement, or supply chain policy was tested.
Those controls would need their own retained evidence and an explicit place in the validation plan.

slides.title: The retained checks exercised health, worker and storage endpoints.

narration.text: The original validation exercised three HTTP endpoints: health, worker, and storage.
Each result belongs to its retained scenario identity and execution record.
The explanation follows those observations without replaying the checks.
An animation of the request path is illustrative, and its playback speed must not be confused with measured execution timing or a captured network trace.

slides.title: Three original HTTP smoke checks passed.

narration.text: All three original HTTP smoke checks passed in this synthetic run.
There were zero recorded failures, zero errors, zero skips, and zero incomplete scenarios.
The presentation preserves those exact totals.
The passing outcomes support the narrow endpoint checks that were executed, while leaving broader authentication and reliability questions open for later validation.

slides.title: Passing checks establish a limited functional baseline.

narration.text: The passing checks establish a limited functional baseline for this proof of concept.
They show that the selected endpoints responded according to the synthetic acceptance expectations.
They do not establish sustained performance, multi-user behavior, failover, or production readiness.
A decision about broader adoption needs those separate questions to be tested and documented with the same evidence discipline.

slides.title: Authentication and production reliability remain unproven.

narration.text: Authenticated workflows and production reliability remain unproven by the available smoke checks.
The report does not contain a successful authenticated user journey or a sustained reliability experiment.
This is a material limitation of the outcome, because a service can respond to a health request while a user-facing workflow still needs additional setup, permissions, or integration work.

slides.title: Validate the remaining workflows before production adoption.

narration.text: The recommendation is to validate the remaining authenticated workflows before production adoption.
Keep the three passing endpoint checks as the current baseline and expand the test plan around the unresolved risks.
Preserve the new outcomes, including failed or incomplete attempts, so that later summaries can explain what changed and what evidence supports the next decision.
